correctness.rationale: For P=c₀…c_{q−1} with distinct q≥3 letters and k≥2 copies, q singleton factors force at least one occurrence of each letter in an attractor, so a size-q candidate chooses one position q t_i+i for each letter. The junction factor c_{q−1}c₀ appears only at internal junctions; if c₀ at absolute 0 and c_{q−1} at qk−1 are both chosen, no chosen occurrence meets any junction. Conversely, any other one-per-letter selection meets an internal junction. Every short factor either lies within a period (met by its chosen start letter) or crosses a junction (met by a selected endpoint), while the union of translated occurrences of any factor of length ≥q is a contiguous interval missing less than q letters at either end; evading that interval would force both forbidden endpoints. Hence exactly k^q−k^{q−2} choices are valid. Independently enumerated all distinct literal factors and every one-per-letter candidate for q=3..5,k=2..4 (1,751 candidates), with no discrepancy. The proof covers all q,k, not merely that finite sweep.
